title: Lexical s-verbs: synes, trives, finnes, møtes and ses
goal: Recognize and use common s-verbs whose s is part of the verb meaning, not a passive ending.

objectives.statement: Recognize and use common s-verbs whose s is part of the verb meaning, not a passive ending.

spans.value: Amir has recently moved to Bergen for work. His colleague Nora asks how he is settling in and suggests meeting after work.

blocks.translation: How do you like living in Bergen?

spans.value: Jeg trives ganske godt, men jeg kjenner ikke så mange her ennå.

blocks.translation: I’m quite happy here, but I don’t know many people here yet.
What do you think of the city?

spans.value: Jeg synes den er fin, særlig når det ikke regner. Finnes det en hyggelig kafé i nærheten?

blocks.translation: I think it is nice, especially when it isn’t raining. Is there a pleasant café nearby?

spans.value: Ja, det finnes en liten kafé ved biblioteket. Vi møtes ofte der etter jobb.

blocks.translation: Yes, there is a small café by the library. We often meet there after work.

spans.value: Det høres bra ut. Skal vi møtes der i morgen?

blocks.translation: That sounds good. Shall we meet there tomorrow?

sections.title: Trives: feeling comfortable in a situation

spans.value: describes feeling comfortable, happy or at ease in a place, group, job or situation. English translations vary because English has no single everyday verb with exactly the same range.

en.value: Amir is happy living in Bergen.
Are you happy at work?

no.value: Barna trives på den nye skolen.

en.value: The children are settling in well at the new school.

no.value: Jeg trives godt sammen med kollegene mine.

en.value: I feel comfortable with my colleagues.
be happy in the city
be happy at work
get along well and feel comfortable with the colleagues
enjoy being together

spans.value: describes someone’s experience of a situation. It is not a passive meaning. In
, nobody is doing an action to Amir.

en.value: Amir is happy at work.

no.value: Amir ansettes av et norsk firma.

en.value: Amir is employed by a Norwegian company.

spans.value: : the company performs the action of employing Amir.

en.value: 'Incorrect: I am happy living in Bergen.'

spans.value: That does not express living happily in Bergen. Use:

en.value: I’m happy living in Bergen.
I like Bergen.

no.value: Jeg liker byen, men jeg trives ikke på jobben.

en.value: I like the city, but I’m not happy at work.

sections.title: Finnes: saying that something exists or is available

no.value: Det finnes en kafé ved biblioteket.

en.value: There is a café by the library.

no.value: Finnes det et apotek i nærheten?

en.value: Is there a pharmacy nearby?

no.value: Det finnes mange turstier rundt Bergen.

en.value: There are many hiking trails around Bergen.
There is no simple solution.
There is an available table.

no.value: Finnes det en buss som går dit?

en.value: Is there a bus that goes there?

spans.value: , do not treat the two as interchangeable.

en.value: I find the café.
There is a café here.

spans.value: In the first sentence, a person finds something. In the second, the café exists or is available in that location.

no.value: Det finner en kafé ved biblioteket.

en.value: 'Not: There is a café by the library. (for the existence meaning)'

no.value: Det finnes en kafé ved biblioteket.

en.value: There is a café by the library.

items.value: when something exists or is available.

no.value: Amir og Nora møtes på kafeen.

en.value: Amir and Nora meet at the café.
We meet after work.
Shall we meet outside the library?
They meet every Friday.
I meet Nora at the café.
Nora meets me at the café.
We meet each other at the café.

spans.value: , the subject meets a person expressed as the object. With
, the subject normally includes the people who meet one another.
This mutual meaning is sometimes called

: two or more participants do the same thing in relation to each other. You do not need to classify every sentence with this term. The practical question is simpler: does the subject include all the people who are meeting?

en.value: 'Incorrect: I’m meeting Nora after work.'
I’m meeting Nora after work.

no.value: Nora og jeg møtes etter jobb.

en.value: Nora and I are meeting after work.
We are meeting after work.

spans.value: with a direct object naming the other participant. Either use
, or include both participants in the subject and use
. It is especially common when people talk about meeting again.

en.value: We often see each other at work.
They see each other almost every day.
When will we see each other again?
See you tomorrow!

spans.value: The last example is extremely common as a farewell. Grammatically,
describes seeing one another, but in context it functions like English

en.value: I see Nora at the café.
Nora sees me at the café.
We see each other at the café.

spans.value: , all participants normally belong in the subject of

en.value: 'Incorrect: I’ll see Nora tomorrow.'
I’ll see Nora tomorrow.

no.value: Nora og jeg ses i morgen.

en.value: Nora and I will see each other tomorrow.
See you tomorrow.

spans.value: focuses on coming together for a meeting or encounter.
focuses on seeing one another and is particularly natural when arranging future contact or saying goodbye.

no.value: Vi møtes på stasjonen klokka åtte.

en.value: We’ll meet at the station at eight.
Great. See you there!
The group meets every Thursday.

no.value: Nå jobber vi i samme bygning, så vi ses ofte.

en.value: Now we work in the same building, so we see each other often.

spans.value: There is overlap in ordinary conversation. The goal is not to force a sharp distinction in every situation. Instead, learn their central uses:

items.value: : arrange or describe a mutual meeting
: see one another; commonly used in farewells and references to future contact

spans.value: Both are complete s-verbs in these meanings. Their
is not simply an instruction to translate them as English passives.
Now compare lexical s-verbs with passive s-forms.

en.value: There is a café here.
The café is closed at six.
We meet outside the café.
The tables are washed every evening.

spans.value: , the full s-verbs carry their established meanings. In
, something is being done to the subject.

items.value: Does the verb mean having an opinion, feeling comfortable, existing, meeting one another or seeing one another?
If so, it is likely one of the lexical s-verbs in this lesson.
Does the sentence instead describe an action being done to the subject?
If so, the form may be passive.

spans.value: This is a meaning distinction, not merely a spelling distinction.
The next day, Amir arrives at the café before Nora. Nora sends him a message.
Beklager, bussen er forsinket. Finnes det et ledig bord?

blocks.translation: Sorry, the bus is delayed. Is there an available table?

spans.value: Ja, jeg har funnet et bord ved vinduet. Jeg synes det er hyggelig her.

blocks.translation: Yes, I’ve found a table by the window. I think it is pleasant here.

spans.value: Så bra! De andre kommer også. Vi møtes der om ti minutter.

blocks.translation: Great! The others are coming too. We’ll meet there in ten minutes.

spans.value: When Nora arrives, she asks about Amir’s first weeks in the city.
Trives du fortsatt i den nye leiligheten?

blocks.translation: Are you still happy in the new apartment?

spans.value: Ja, og naboene er hyggelige. Vi ses ofte i oppgangen.

blocks.translation: Yes, and the neighbours are pleasant. We often see each other in the stairwell.

spans.value: The same five verbs now serve a connected purpose:
None of these sentences has a passive meaning.
Maja has started an evening course. She is writing to her friend Jonas about it. The school, classmates and plans are new, but the same s-verbs remain useful.

en.value: I’m happy on the course.
I think the teacher explains clearly.

no.value: Det finnes et stille leserom i andre etasje.

en.value: There is a quiet reading room on the second floor.
The class meets there before the lesson.

no.value: Jonas og jeg går på forskjellige kurs, men vi ses i pausen.

en.value: Jonas and I attend different courses, but we see each other during the break.

prompt.value: Classify each Norwegian sentence by the meaning of its s-ending verb. Use the specific bucket that fits the whole sentence; do not classify from the final -s alone.

explanation.value: Lexical s-verbs such as synes, trives, finnes, møtes, and ses have their own meanings; the -s does not automatically mark a passive.

prompt.value: Write a short connected message in Norwegian to Jonas about Maja and her evening course. Use each of synes, trives, finnes, møtes, and ses exactly once as a complete lexical verb. Give an opinion about the course, say how Maja feels in the group, mention something that exists or is available at the school, and describe when the classmates meet and when Maja and Jonas see one another. For every meeting or seeing statement, include all mutual participants in its subject.
